thesis: The edd_retry fallback re-runs the same EDD heuristic that just failed at the cap, burning ~20s without progress; replacing edd_retry with an immediate forced-permutation jump will free ~18s for SA on bench_B5 hard instances.
rationale_short: Eval Run #2 shows all 4 seeds fail at the 2.26s init_check_limit cap on bench_B5_b120/b150, then myalgorithm.py:608-625 re-invokes evaluate_permutation(EDD, hard_deadline-safety_margin) which produces no feasible result before finally calling evaluate_forced_permutation. Since EDD already failed identically, the second attempt only differs in budget but the same _place_blocks->_repair pipeline is structurally stuck (stage 2). Skipping straight to forced gives SA ~18-20s of wall-clock on these instances.
ogc_assumption_dep: forced-fallback via _empty_bay_entry guarantees stage 2/3 pass when bay is empty
ogc_assumption_break_risk: none - we are removing a no-op step; forced fallback still runs and is structurally guaranteed feasible per baseline_greedy._force_place docstring.

expected_impact.smoke: neutral (smoke seeds succeed; edd_retry branch never runs)
expected_impact.bench_hard: SA iterations rise from 0 to >=3 on bench_B5_b120/b150; obj may improve 5-15% via 1-2 SA improvements over the forced solution
expected_impact.feasibility: no change - forced fallback remains the safety net

thesis: Adding `repair_mode='simple'` as a structurally-guaranteed seed before the SA loop converts the 'all seeds infeasible' regime into 'one feasible seed in <3s', restoring SA wall-clock and providing a non-trivial starting objective better than _force_place's degenerate (0,0) layout.
rationale_short: baseline_greedy._repair with repair_mode='simple' uses _empty_bay_entry to push violating blocks into bay-empty time windows (lines 794-838) — this is structurally guaranteed feasible (same proof as _force_place) but preserves the greedy's spatial placement for non-violating blocks. Running it once as the first seed on EDD costs ~1-2s on n=120 and yields a feasible solution with objective much better than _force_place because only the 5-20 stage-2-violating blocks get pushed, not all 120. This decouples 'we have a feasible solution' from 'we found a great heuristic'.
ogc_assumption_dep: _empty_bay_entry guarantees stage 2/3 pass when bay is empty during [entry, exit_t)
monkey-patches active during _place_blocks but restored before return
ogc_assumption_break_risk: Stage 4 (spatial collision) risk: simple-repair sets x,y=0,0 only when result['stage']==4 (line 822). If the first failure is stage 2 but pushing to empty window exposes a stage 4 elsewhere later, repair could loop. Mitigated because max_passes=10 and falls through to forced path. 'none' for stage 2 specifically.
target_locus: baseline/myalgorithm.py:algorithm:582-606 (insert simple-repair seed before the portfolio loop) and 489-543 (add a simple-mode variant of evaluate_permutation)

expected_impact.smoke: neutral (existing seeds already feasible; simple-seed runs but loses to SlackRatio's objective)
expected_impact.bench_hard: feasibility guaranteed in <3s on bench_B5_b120/b150; SA gets >=15s budget; bench_B5_b120 obj drops from 14.3M toward forced fallback's level OR better; bench_B5_b150 from 32.6M
expected_impact.feasibility: strictly improved on hard instances - no more reliance on forced fallback path

thesis: The 2.26s wall-time observed for every failing seed equals init_check_limit=timelimit*0.30/4=2.25s, meaning seeds are time-cut not search-exhausted; raising the per-seed budget for failing seeds via a two-tier retry (1s probe, then 8s deepen if probe shows progress) will let _repair converge on at least one seed and skip the fallback entirely.
rationale_short: myalgorithm.py:580 computes init_check_limit = max(0.5, timelimit*0.30/max(1,len(target_heuristics))) = 30*0.30/4 = 2.25s, matching the reported 2.26s exactly. _repair's max_passes=10 is rarely reached in 2.25s on n=120 with custom_check_entry/exit per pass. If the greedy is 'almost' feasible (e.g. 5-10 violating blocks), giving it 8s would likely converge; if it's far (50+ violations), it will burn 8s with no gain — so the two-tier probe (run cheap, peek at viol count, decide to deepen) bounds the downside.
ogc_assumption_dep: check_feasibility violation counts are stable across passes when bay state is rebuilt
_repair greedy mode handles cycles via forced_ids (line 847)
ogc_assumption_break_risk: none. We're tuning timeouts, not the physical model. Risk is wall-clock budget allocation only.
target_locus: baseline/myalgorithm.py:algorithm:578-606 (replace fixed init_check_limit with a two-tier probe-then-deepen loop)

expected_impact.bench_hard: one seed converges feasible within 10s on bench_B5_b120 OR remains infeasible -> falls to H-001/H-002 path; if converges, bench_B5_b120 obj drops 10-30% vs forced
expected_impact.feasibility: no degradation; falls through to existing fallback if probe shows no progress

thesis: In Athena's algorithm(), the release_time fallback pass only runs when the first (smoothing/target_entry-based) place_initial pass is INFEASIBLE; it never runs when the first pass is feasible-but-poor. Making the fallback objective-comparative (run it whenever the first pass's tardiness is non-trivial, then keep min-objective of the two inits) recovers the mid-difficulty regressions introduced by the cause-1 fix without giving up the b200 win.
rationale_short: The cause-1 fix (_find_earliest_slot future-entry blocking widened from `entry < a` to `entry <= a`, commit 7d5326b) made the first place_initial pass succeed on instances that previously fell through to the release_time fallback. Comparing run 7 (sha f312ec3+dirty) -> run 8 (7d5326b): my_B5_b200_hard improved 50.1M->11.7M (-77%, tardiness 16678->3895) because it stopped collapsing to the tardiness-blind all_forced path. BUT bench_B5_b150_mixed_hard regressed 3.18M->4.55M (+43%) and bench_B4_b70_dense_geometry 478k->676k (+42%): their init.done flipped from infeasible-1st-pass (then release_time fallback init 3.19M/489k) to feasible-1st-pass (target_entry init 4.56M/851k), so the better-tardiness release_time fallback is now skipped and SA cannot close the gap in budget. The fallback branch at algorithm():1869 only triggers on `not init_res['feasible']`, so a feasible-but-high-tardiness 1st pass is accepted without comparison.
ogc_assumption_dep: smooth_time_windows target_entry is load-flattening biased and pushes entry later than release_time, raising tardiness on some instances
_force_place/_empty_bay_entry all_forced path is tardiness-blind (serializes per bay)
official check_feasibility 5-stage ordering; place_initial assembly can still fail stage 2 from order-dependent greedy on the densest instances
ogc_assumption_break_risk: none - this only adds a second constructive pass + min(objective) selection; both candidate inits are already validated by check_feasibility before SA. No change to the physical model or the slot-finder.
target_locus: baseline/my_new_algorithm.py:algorithm:1869-1889 (the `if not init_res['feasible']` fallback block) - change the trigger from feasibility-only to objective-comparative, and keep the min-objective init across the target_entry pass and the release_time pass.

expected_impact.smoke: neutral (smoke inits already near-optimal; second pass either matches or is discarded by min-objective)
expected_impact.bench_hard: bench_B5_b150_mixed_hard recovers toward 3.18M; bench_B4_b70_dense_geometry toward 478k; my_B5_b200_hard preserved (first pass already best there, ~11.7M)
expected_impact.feasibility: no change - all_forced safety net retained

thesis: On large/dense instances (n>=120) the destroy-repair 'large' move is the only operator that can relieve same-bay time-congestion (the dominant w1*tardiness source), but it is throttled to ~12% in the balanced profile and only one of four workers (large_repair, 35%) emphasizes it; making the large-move share scale up with n_blocks will lift SA gain on b150/b200 from ~0% toward the 20-25% seen on mid-size instances.
rationale_short: Run 8 events show SA improvement over init collapsing with scale: bench_B3_b30 99.6%, b50 24.9%, b70 20.6%, b120 6.6%, b150 0.20% (4.560M->4.552M), my_B5_b200 0.012% (11.710M->11.709M), despite parallel_sa.start reporting 45.8s/39.9s remaining budget on b150/b200. Small/medium moves are single-block entry/orient/bay perturbations (_do_small_move/_do_medium_move) that cannot move a block earlier when its bay timeline is densely packed (horizon ~27 with 200 blocks over 5 bays); only _apply_large_move (line 1057) destroys tardy blocks and sweep-repairs, but SA_PROFILES gives it only 12% (balanced) / 35% (large_repair, 1 of 4 workers) and that mix is static in n. obj is tardiness-dominated (w1=3000; b200 obj1=3895*3000~=11.7M of 11.71M total).
ogc_assumption_dep: _apply_large_move re-runs _find_earliest_slot + _force_place which respect the j>=k descent rule and 5-stage check
each large move is fully re-validated by evaluate_solution before accept (line 1592), so feasibility is preserved
worker profiles are independent multi-start trajectories; raising large-share on a subset does not affect the others
ogc_assumption_break_risk: none - this only reweights existing, already-validated move operators. No change to the slot finder, the descent-rule collision check, or the operations-dict EXIT-before-ENTRY ordering. Risk is purely budget: large moves cost a full evaluate_solution, so too-high a share could lower total iterations.
target_locus: baseline/my_new_algorithm.py:SA_PROFILES (1299-1328) + sa_loop:1517-1583 (the p_small_cut/p_medium_cut derivation) - make move_probs n_blocks-adaptive, e.g. for n>=120 shift balanced from (0.55,0.88) toward (0.45,0.70) so large-share rises 12%->30%, and/or assign >=2 of 4 workers a large-heavy profile.

expected_impact.smoke: neutral (smoke already reaches ~optimal via small moves; large-share bump runs but converges to same near-zero obj)
expected_impact.bench_hard: bench_B5_b150_mixed_hard SA gain >5% (total_obj < 4.3M vs 4.55M); my_B5_b200_hard SA gain >2% (total_obj < 11.45M vs 11.71M); bench_B5_b120 gain rises above 6.6%
expected_impact.feasibility: no change - large move is fully re-checked; init all_forced safety net retained

thesis: place_initial's sequential best-fit sweep consumes 15.3s of the 60s budget on my_B5_b200_hard (and 9.4s on b150), leaving SA workers only ~40s/46s; time-boxing the init via a tighter bay_cands_cap/pos_cands_cap for n>=150 returns ~5-8s to SA, and per H-005's evidence that wall-clock is the binding SA constraint on large instances, this directly buys additional large-move iterations.
rationale_short: athena.init.done.elapsed scales steeply with n: 0.3s (b30) -> 1.7s (b70) -> 5.0s (b120) -> 9.4s (b150) -> 15.3s (b200), while parallel_sa.start.remaining drops to 45.8s/39.9s on b150/b200. place_initial (line 454) evaluates bay_cands_cap=4 bays x pos_cands_cap=12 positions x _find_earliest_slot per block, twice (target_entry pass then release_time pass), all single-threaded in the main process before any worker starts. On the instances where SA already yields ~0% gain, every second of init is a second SA cannot use; cutting init to ~8s on b200 gives the 4 workers ~7s more each.
ogc_assumption_dep: place_initial still produces a feasible (or all_forced) assignment at lower caps; _force_place safety net (line 536) covers any block the narrowed search misses
SA workers start from this single init; a slightly worse init is acceptable if SA has more budget to improve it (couples to H-005)
check_feasibility 5-stage validation still gates the init before parallel_sa
ogc_assumption_break_risk: Quality risk, not feasibility: narrowing caps could raise init n_forced > 0 on the densest instances, and forced placements are tardiness-blind (serialize per bay), so init objective rises. Mitigated by keeping caps unchanged for n<150 and verifying n_forced stays 0; if forced placements appear, the SA-budget gain must outweigh the worse init.
target_locus: baseline/my_new_algorithm.py:algorithm:1852-1866 (the place_initial call site) - pass n-adaptive caps, e.g. bay_cands_cap=3, pos_cands_cap=8 when n>=150; alternatively add a deadline-fraction cap so init never exceeds ~0.15*timelimit.

expected_impact.smoke: neutral (init already <1s; caps unchanged for small n)
expected_impact.bench_hard: athena.init.done.elapsed on my_B5_b200_hard drops from 15.3s to <=10s; parallel_sa.start.remaining rises above 45s; with the extra budget total_obj on b200 <= 11.6M and b150 <= 4.4M (modest alone; multiplicative with H-005)
expected_impact.feasibility: no change expected; n_forced must remain 0 (rollback trigger if not)

thesis: Make smooth_time_windows objective-aware by scaling tardiness and release-delay penalties with w1 and slack, so smoothed target_entry absorbs the useful part of release-time fallback without spending a second full init pass on dense instances.
rationale_short: Training_set analysis showed every block has slack<=10 and w1 is 8889..29630, but smooth_time_windows used fixed gamma_tard=4.0. Run #39 vs #35 improved full training_set total 987.09M -> 856.66M (-13.2%) with 20/20 feasible and no regression in the fair full-run comparison.

thesis: Inside place_initial, run release_time second-pass rescue for blocks whose target-entry placement is tardy, so block-level rescue captures fallback benefits without a full second seed.

A narrower condition had the same failure mode.
